correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the Galois derivation with empty-intersection conventions. For any k=floor((1-eps)ln r/lambda), the binomial supporting-row mean exceeds r^eps; a Chernoff bound and independence of unexposed columns prove all k-subsets closed with summable failure. Every concept with small extent or intent is counted by its projection, and every large-large concept corresponds injectively to an all-one rectangle; its first moment has exponent (1-eps^2)(ln r)(ln m)/lambda, yielding a summable upper tail. Borel–Cantelli then yields the asserted a.s. limit without cross-size independence. The same expectation sandwich works. A standalone exact-rational checker evaluated 42 exhaustive finite Bernoulli incidence cases and the extent–intent bijection; finite checking is not offered as a proof of the infinite statement.

value.rationale: For a standard formal-concept coin-toss null model, the theorem identifies the exact first-order exponent of the typical concept count in every polynomial rectangular regime, instead of a worst-case exponential bound or an expected-value lower bound. Simultaneous closure of all subcritical logarithmic attribute sets is a structural strengthening useful for understanding genuine concept growth. It supplies a sharp benchmark for output-sensitive enumeration and data-model comparisons; it does not claim exact runtime or second-order fluctuations.
